docs.b: Accessibility statement Everyone should be able to use this site For a long time now, our door in Clear Lake has been open to everyone who walks in. We want this website to feel the same way. Eye Trends Vision & Glasses Center, led by Dr. Jerry Hyder, offers comprehensive eye care and optical for Clear Lake and the greater Houston area, and we want every neighbor to be able to use this site comfortably and reach us however they browse. That is the same welcome we give you in person. On this page How we build this site The standard we aim for Trouble using this page? Tell us. An honest, ongoing effort. This is an honest, ongoing effort, not a finished checklist. We work on the site the way we work with patients: we keep looking for what could be better, and we fix the gaps we find. We are not claiming the site is perfect or fully barrier-free, and we hold no accessibility certification. What we can tell you is that we take this seriously and keep at it. How we build this site We build this site to be modern, clean, and calm to use, with the same unhurried feeling we aim for in the exam room. In plain terms, that means generous whitespace so pages never feel crowded, legible type at a comfortable size, and clear contrast between the words and the background so text is easy to read. Links tell you where they go instead of just saying "click here." The fields on our booking and contact forms are labeled, so it is clear what each one is asking for. You can move through the navigation with a keyboard, not only a mouse. And the images that carry real meaning include descriptive alt text, so a screen reader can describe them out loud. The standard we aim for We work toward the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), the widely recognized standard for making websites usable by as many people as possible. We try to apply it across the whole site, not only the main pages. The navigation, the forms you use to reach us, and the footer with our address, phone number, hours, and legal links are held to that same standard, because those are the parts you rely on to actually get in touch and book a visit. Trouble using this page? Tell us. If any part of this site gets in your way, or you need something on it in a different form, tell us and we will help you get what you need. A real person answers. Call us at (281) 488-0066 , or stop by 515 Bay Area Blvd #300, Houston, TX 77058. You can also reach us through our contact page , and we will take it from there.

Kids' vision · Featured Featured guide · 5 min read Kids' vision in Clear Lake - what parents should watch for, and when a squint or a headache means it is time for an exam. If you have ever watched your child sit too close to the screen, rub their eyes after homework, or come home with headaches, you already know the worry. Most of the time it is nothing serious. Sometimes it is a sign their eyes need a little help. This guide walks through the everyday things parents notice - squinting, tilting the head, losing their place while reading, eyes that drift or cross - and tells you plainly which ones can wait for a routine check and which ones are worth a call. We see children here from about age 4 or 5, and families come back year after year to have their kids' eyes checked as their vision changes. If something does need attention, we can usually find a time that works - we hold Saturday morning hours, and we keep room for same-day visits when a child's eye is red, hurting, or clearly not right. You do not have to figure out on your own whether it can wait. Read the parent's guide Book an eye exam for your child The library The whole library, in plain language. docs.b: Senior eye exams, Clear Lake Unhurried senior eye exams in Clear Lake, from a doctor who has watched Bay Area eyes for decades Senior eye exams in Clear Lake: we take Medicare, and we give your eyes the time a thorough exam actually takes. After 65, your eyes deserve more than a quick prescription check. They deserve a doctor who sits down, looks closely, and dilates when that is the right call. Eye Trends is a full-service one-stop optometry practice here in Clear Lake, offering comprehensive and medical eye exams, contact lenses, and designer eyewear, all in the same place with Dr. Jerry Hyder. You book once, and everything your eyes need is under one roof. Glaucoma, macular degeneration, and an early cataract usually give no warning you can feel, so they go unnoticed until vision is already slipping. By the time something looks off, the change has often been building for a while. That is exactly what a rushed fifteen-minute visit for a glasses update tends to miss. A fast screening refreshes a prescription and sends you on your way, but it does not take the time to look closely enough to catch the health change happening underneath. Eye Trends is for Clear Lake and Bay Area families and adults who want thorough, personal eye care from a doctor who takes the time, rather than a rushed fix. When the goal is catching a small change early, while it is still treatable, the looking is the whole point. What you get Three things you can count on 01 An unhurried, dilated exam, with time to be heard We talk, we visit, and we work through your eyes without watching the clock. When it is the right call, we dilate so we can see the health of your eyes clearly, and you have the time to ask every question and get a real answer. 02 Year-over-year monitoring of your eye health Dr. Hyder does not just update a prescription; he monitors and manages the health of your eyes over time. Because he remembers last year's baseline, he can see what has actually changed and what is simply you, and follow it before it becomes a problem. 03 Plain-language answers about what is happening You leave knowing what is going on with your eyes and what to do next, explained the way a person can follow. No jargon, no rush, no wondering what the doctor meant. Inside the exam Inside a thorough senior exam A senior eye exam here screens for the age-related conditions that matter most, each step explained as we go: Cataract evaluation. A dilated look at the lens of the eye, so Dr. Hyder can see a cataract clearly and judge how far along it is. Glaucoma testing. We check the pressure inside your eyes and take a careful look at the health of the optic nerve, an important early-warning part of the exam. Macular degeneration (AMD) check. We evaluate the macula at the back of the eye, where age-related changes to your central vision first show up. Diabetic-retinopathy screening. For patients with diabetes, we look closely at the retina for the changes diabetes can cause. An up-to-date prescription. You still walk out with a current prescription for glasses or contact lenses, in the same visit. If a cataract has progressed to the point where surgery is the right step, Dr. Hyder handles the evaluation and the pre-op and post-op care, and coordinates the procedure with a trusted surgeon. That is co-management: the surgery itself is done in the surgeon's hands, never in our office, and the care around it stays with the doctor who already knows your eyes. Start with a comprehensive exam 42 years in Clear Lake Why older patients trust us Caring for Clear Lake eyes since 1984 Dr. Jerry Hyder has cared for Clear Lake and Bay Area families for 42 years, in the same practice since 1984. Many of those patients have stayed with him for decades. That kind of history is the real reason an older patient can trust this practice for the long haul: when the doctor already knows your eyes, he can spot the subtle change a stranger would miss. We will always lead with that continuity rather than a detection rate or a success number we cannot stand behind. Eye Trends is a full-service one-stop optometry practice in Clear Lake, and Dr. Jerry Hyder handles it all under one roof, comprehensive and medical eye care, contacts, and designer eyewear. You have astigmatism, or you have hit the age where reading up close has changed, or your prescription is simply demanding, and you get handed a standard soft lens. By mid-afternoon it has dried out. It blurs. It never quite sits where it should. After a round or two of that, most people give up and decide contacts are not for their eyes. The lens was the problem, not your eyes. A soft lens off the shelf is built for the average eye, and a harder-to-fit eye is not average. That is the kind of patient we built this practice around: Clear Lake and Bay Area families and adults who want thorough, personal eye care from a doctor who takes the time, rather than a rushed big-box fix. We will not throw a made-up statistic at you about how common this is, we will just take the time to find the lens that fits. What changes Three things the right specialty lens gives you Not a stock lens off a shelf. A lens matched to your eye, comfort that holds all day, and a doctor who keeps refining the fit until it is right. 01 A lens matched to your actual eye We fit the lens to the real shape and movement of your eye, not to an average off a chart. That is the whole difference between a lens that fights you all day and one you forget you are wearing. 02 Comfortable, stable vision through the whole day The goal is not "clear for the first hour." It is clear and comfortable at 9 in the morning and still clear and comfortable at 6 at night, so you stop planning your day around when the lenses give out. 03 A doctor who adjusts the fit until it is right This is unhurried care, not a fifteen-minute counter visit. Dr. Hyder takes the time to measure and fit, and then refines the lens over calm follow-ups instead of settling for "close enough." We talk, we visit, and we keep at it until the fit is right on your eye. What we fit The three specialty lenses we fit, and how the fitting works Toric lenses for astigmatism , soft lenses built to hold their orientation so astigmatism does not blur back in through the day. Gas-permeable (GP) rigid lenses for demanding prescriptions , custom-ordered rigid lenses that keep their shape on the eye and correct a strong or difficult prescription more precisely than a soft lens usually manages. Multifocal lenses for presbyopia , one lens that carries both near and far, so you can read a menu and see across the room without reaching for readers. Every one of these starts the same way: careful measurement of the curvature and surface of your cornea, a trial lens on the eye so we can watch how it centers and moves each time you blink, and follow-up visits to confirm the comfort and the clarity both hold. We fit toric, gas-permeable, and multifocal lenses, and those three fittings cover the large majority of the difficult prescriptions we see. Some eyes, an irregular or surgically-changed cornea, for instance, need a specialty lens that falls outside those three fittings. That kind of lens is outside our scope, and if your eyes need it we will tell you honestly and point you to the right specialist rather than guess at it.
